children: BEML Limited has secured a ₹5,400 crore contract to supply and maintain 16 high-speed trains for the Mumbai–Ahmedabad High Speed Rail (MAHSR) corridor, marking the largest single order in the company’s history and taking its overall order book beyond ₹21,000 crore.

The contract from the National High Speed Rail Corporation Limited (NHSRCL) is a major breakthrough for BEML’s high-speed rail ambitions, placing the Indian engineering and manufacturing company among a select group of global players with capabilities to develop and manufacture high-speed rolling stock.
These train-sets have to be delivered in the next 7-8 years, official sources told thebusinessline.

For BEML, the ₹5,400 crore NHSRCL order represents more than a jump in its order book. It gives the company a significant opportunity to establish itself in one of the most technologically demanding segments of the global rail industry. This order takes BEML’s overall order book beyond ₹21,000 crore.
The NHSRCL contract builds on BEML’s ongoing ₹866.87 crore programme with Integral Coach Factory (ICF), Chennai) for two indigenous high-speed trainsets, each comprising eight coaches.
These train sets are being developed at BEML’s Aditya High-Speed Rail Complex in Bengaluru, a dedicated 10-acre facility built for the company’s high-speed rail programme.

The B-28 trainsets are being engineered for speeds of up to 280 kmph, with delivery scheduled for early 2027. The fully air-conditioned Chair Car trains will feature reclining and rotatable seats, facilities for passengers with restricted mobility and onboard infotainment systems.

The Aditya complex is designed as a specialised manufacturing hub for high-speed rolling stock, equipped with robotic laser welding systems, universal hydraulic jigs and integrated mechanical and electrical outfitting facilities.
The facility is intended to give BEML the engineering and manufacturing infrastructure needed to move beyond prototypes and participate in the larger high-speed rail ecosystem.
The complex was inaugurated by Union Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw, highlighting the strategic importance attached to developing domestic capabilities in advanced rail manufacturing.
The shares of BEML Ltd surged 6.02 per cent on the BSE on Friday to close at ₹2,134.25 apiece.

title: BEML bags ₹5,400 cr order for 16 high-speed trains for Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train corridor
